title: RegisterReady: landlord database registration and certificate tracking for small letting agents
summary: England's new landlord database ("Register your rental property") opens region by region from 15 December 2026, and every rented home must be registered by November 2027 with safety information. Small letting agents and landlords with a few properties must collect and keep this data current. RegisterReady reads certificates, finds gaps and reminds before anything expires.
hook: "We manage 180 properties for 90 landlords. Half the gas certificates are in someone's email. Now every one has to go on a government register."
story:
**Lucy runs a small letting agency in Birmingham** that manages **180 homes for 90 landlords**. The West Midlands is the first region where the new database opens, on 15 December 2026, and existing landlords there have **three months** to register. Each entry needs landlord and property details plus safety information: the **gas safety certificate, electrical report (EICR) and EPC**.

Her CRM holds the tenancy data, but certificates sit in emails and shared folders, and some landlords handle their own gas checks. Giving false information or letting entries lapse can lead to Rent Repayment Orders. She needs a tool that reads every certificate, shows what is missing or expiring and prepares the data for each registration.
whyNow: The PRS database launches on 15 December 2026 in the West Midlands and rolls out across England over 12 months; all private rented properties must be registered by 14 November 2027, with an annual fee. Tenancy reforms under the Renters' Rights Act already started on 1 May 2026, and councils have stronger enforcement powers.
evidence: The database ("Register your rental property") starts on 15 December 2026 in the West Midlands, then other regions over 12 months [HCR Law / Bevan Brittan]
Landlords generally get three months after their region opens; all properties must be registered by 14 November 2027 [Bevan Brittan]
Registration will be mandatory with an annual fee still to be confirmed, and will include gas, electrical and EPC information [JLL]
False or misleading information, or failing to keep entries active, can lead to a Rent Repayment Order [Womble Bond Dickinson]
Gas safety checks are needed every 12 months and EICRs every five years [council guidance, e.g. Derby City Council]

whyReal.title: Hard deadline, every property
whyReal.text: Every private rented home in England must be on the register by November 2027, region by region from December 2026.

whyReal.title: Data is scattered
whyReal.text: Certificates live in emails, landlord folders and contractor portals. Agents must collect them for hundreds of homes in three months.

whyReal.title: Penalties hit agents' clients
whyReal.text: Wrong or lapsed entries can lead to Rent Repayment Orders, so landlords will expect agents to get it right.

whyReal.title: Reuses the document engine
whyReal.text: Reading certificates and tracking expiry is the same engine as SubDocs and CredTrack, pointed at a new deadline.

solution.title: Bulk upload
solution.text: drop in folders or forward emails with certificates; AI reads property address, type, engineer, date and expiry.

solution.title: Match to properties
solution.text: certificates are matched to the property list from the CRM export.

solution.title: Gap report
solution.text: shows which homes miss a gas certificate, EICR or EPC, or have one expiring soon.

solution.title: Chase
solution.text: sends landlords and contractors a link to upload what is missing.

solution.title: Registration pack
solution.text: prepares the data for each property's registration and reminds when entries need updating.
